arxiv-1904-07578.title: Small Gauge Transformations and Universal Geometry in Heterotic Theories
arxiv-1904-07578.creator: Jock MCORIST † and Roberto SISCA ‡
arxiv-1904-07578.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Jock MCORIST † and Roberto SISCA ‡. The first part of this paper describes in detail the action of small gauge transformations in heterotic supergravity. We show a convenient gauge fixing is ‘holomorphic gauge’ together with a condition on the holomorphic top form. This gauge fixing, combined with supersymmetry and the Bianchi identity, allows us to determine a set of non-linear PDEs for the terms in the Hodge decomposition.

arxiv-2012-10665.title: CONTROLLABILITY OF NETWORKED SYSTEM WITH HETEROGENEOUS DYNAMICS
arxiv-2012-10665.creator: Abhijith Ajayakumar and Raju K. George Department of Mathematics, Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology, Thiruvananthapuram 695 547, India. Corresponding author: abhijithajayakumar.19@res.iist.ac.in
arxiv-2012-10665.description: Abstract In this paper, a necessary and sufficient condition for the controllability of networked systems with heterogeneous dynamics is established where the nodes are higher dimensional linear time invariant(LTI) systems and the network topology is directed and weighted. The controllability of networked system over some specific topologies are also examined and some non-controllability results are obtained.

arxiv-2105-14949.title: Dixmier traces, Wodzicki residues, and determinants on compact Lie groups: the paradigm of the global quantisation Thanks: The authors are supported by the FWO Odysseus 1 grant G.0H94.18N: Analysis and Partial Differential Equations and by the Methusalem programme of the Ghent University Special Res
arxiv-2105-14949.creator: Duván Cardona, Julio Delgado, Michael Ruzhansky
arxiv-2105-14949.description: Abstract . By following the paradigm of the global quantisation, instead of the analysis under changes of coordinates, in this work we establish a global analysis for the explicit computation of the Dixmier trace and the Wodzicki residue of (elliptic and subelliptic) pseudo-differential operators on compact Lie groups. The regularised determinant for the Dixmier trace is also computed.

arxiv-2106-14348.title: An Augmented Lagrangian Deep Learning Method for Variational Problems with Essential Boundary Conditions Corresponding author.
arxiv-2106-14348.creator: Jianguo Huang ( jghuang@sjtu.edu.cn )
arxiv-2106-14348.description: Abstract This paper is concerned with a novel deep learning method for variational problems with essential boundary conditions. To this end, we first reformulate the original problem into a minimax problem corresponding to a feasible augmented Lagrangian, which can be solved by the augmented Lagrangian method in an infinite dimensional setting.

arxiv-2212-01838.title: Automata Learning meets Shielding
arxiv-2212-01838.creator: Martin Tappler, Stefan Pranger, Bettina Könighofer, Edi Muškardin, Roderick Bloem, Kim Larsen
arxiv-2212-01838.description: Abstract Safety is still one of the major research challenges in reinforcement learning (RL). In this paper, we address the problem of how to avoid safety violations of RL agents during exploration in probabilistic and partially unknown environments. Our approach combines automata learning for Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) and shield synthesis in an iterative approach.

arxiv-2303-08979.title: An Approximate Bayesian Approach to Covariate-dependent Graphical Modeling
arxiv-2303-08979.creator: Sutanoy Dasgupta, Peng Zhao, Jacob Helwig, Prasenjit Ghosh, Debdeep Pati and Bani K. Mallick Department of Statistics, Texas A&M University
arxiv-2303-08979.description: Abstract Gaussian graphical models typically assume a homogeneous structure across all subjects, which is often restrictive in applications. In this article, we propose a weighted pseudo-likelihood approach for graphical modeling which allows different subjects to have different graphical structures depending on extraneous covariates. The pseudo-likelihood approach replaces the joint distribution by a product of the conditional distributions of each variable.

arxiv-2410-01823.title: Refining Calculus Pedagogy
arxiv-2410-01823.creator: Parthasarathy Srinivasan
arxiv-2410-01823.description: Abstract There have been several modifications of how basic calculus has been taught, but very few of these modifications have considered the computational tools available at our disposal. Here, we present a few tools that are easy to develop and use.

arxiv-2501-17355.title: The time-dependent reproduction number for epidemics in heterogeneous populations
arxiv-2501-17355.creator: Ioana Bouros, Robin N. Thompson, David Gavaghan, Ben Lambert
arxiv-2501-17355.description: Abstract The time-dependent reproduction number R t R_{t} can be used to track pathogen transmission and to assess the efficacy of interventions. This quantity can be estimated by fitting renewal equation models to time series of infectious disease case counts. These models almost invariably assume a homogeneous population.

arxiv-2503-17366.title: Photoluminescence from metal nanostructures - dependence on size
arxiv-2503-17366.creator: Imon Kalyan, Ieng Wai Un, Gilles Rosolen, Nir Shitrit, Yonatan Sivan
arxiv-2503-17366.description: Abstract For decades, there have been multiple seemingly contradicting experimental reports on the dependence of the photoluminescence from metal nanostructures on their size. We reconcile these reports using a simple analytic formula which is found to match well photoluminescence measurements for a range of structures and illumination conditions.

arxiv-2505-07215.title: Measuring General Intelligence with Generated Games
arxiv-2505-07215.creator: Vivek Verma, David Huang, William Chen, Dan Klein, Nicholas Tomlin, Computer Science Divison
arxiv-2505-07215.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Vivek Verma, David Huang, William Chen, Dan Klein, Nicholas Tomlin, Computer Science Divison. We present gg-bench , a collection of game environments designed to evaluate general reasoning capabilities in language models. Unlike most static benchmarks, gg-bench is a data generating process where new evaluation instances can be generated at will.

arxiv-2507-12624.title: Pathology-Guided Virtual Staining Metric for Evaluation and Training
arxiv-2507-12624.creator: Qiankai Wang, James E.D. Tweel, Parsin Haji Reza, Anita Layton
arxiv-2507-12624.description: Abstract Virtual staining has emerged as a powerful alternative to traditional histopathological staining techniques, enabling rapid, reagent-free image transformations. However, existing evaluation methods predominantly rely on full-reference image quality assessment (FR-IQA) metrics such as structural similarity, which are originally designed for natural images and often fail to capture pathology-relevant features.

arxiv-2507-15290.title: Feel-Good Thompson Sampling for Contextual Bandits: a Markov Chain Monte Carlo Showdown
arxiv-2507-15290.creator: Emile AnandGeorgia Institute of TechnologySchool of Computer ScienceAtlanta, GA, 30308 emile@gatech.edu, Sarah LiawCalifornia Institute of TechnologyComputing + Mathematical Sciences DepartmentPasadena, CA, 02138 sliaw@caltech.edu
arxiv-2507-15290.description: Abstract Thompson Sampling (TS) is widely used to address the exploration/exploitation tradeoff in contextual bandits, yet recent theory shows that it does not explore aggressively enough in high-dimensional problems. Feel-Good Thompson Sampling (FG-TS) addresses this by adding an optimism bonus that biases toward high-reward models, and it achieves the asymptotically minimax-optimal regret in the linear setting when posteriors are exact.

arxiv-2510-08304.title: Bayesian Profile Regression with Linear Mixed Models (Profile-LMM) applied to Longitudinal Exposome Data
arxiv-2510-08304.creator: Matteo Amestoy \ORCID 0000-0002-2032-1448, Mark van de Wiel, Jeroen Lakerveld, Wessel van Wieringen
arxiv-2510-08304.description: Abstract Exposure to diverse non-genetic factors, known as the exposome, is a critical determinant of health outcomes. However, analyzing the exposome presents significant methodological challenges, including: high collinearity among exposures, the longitudinal nature of repeated measurements, and potential complex interactions with individual characteristics.

catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acuas.title: Acuas (Catholic Encyclopedia article)
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acuas.creator: John Joseph A'Becket
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acuas.description: Article 'Acuas' from the Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), the 15-volume English-language reference work published 1907-1914 by Robert Appleton Company.

plos-pone-0007008.creator: Ruth I. Johnson, Ross L. Cagan
plos-pone-0007008.description: PLOS ONE research article. The Drosophila pupal eye has become a popular paradigm for understanding morphogenesis and tissue patterning. Correct rearrangement of cells between ommatidia is required to organize the ommatidial array across the eye field. This requires cell movement, cell death, changes to ce

pmc-10622537.title: Generation of a helper phage for the fluorescent detection of peptide-target interactions by dual-display phages
pmc-10622537.creator: Laura Maria De Plano, Salvatore Oddo, Salvatore P P Guglielmino, Antonella Caccamo, Sabrina Conoci
pmc-10622537.description: Phage display is a molecular biology technique that allows the presentation of foreign peptides on the surface of bacteriophages. It is widely utilized for applications such as the discovery of biomarkers, the development of therapeutic antibodies, and the investigation of protein–protein interactions.

pmc-11600859.title: Characterization of Bacteroides fragilis from the vagina of a giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca) with vaginitis
pmc-11600859.creator: Chanjuan Yue, Xiaoping Ma, Wanjing Yang, Yiyan Liu, Zhisong Yang, Rong Hou, Xia Yan, Mei Yang, Xiaoyan Su, Songrui Liu
pmc-11600859.description: BackgroundBacteroides fragilis is a prevalent anaerobic bacterium typically resides in the human vagina. It is known to potentially induce infections under specific conditions. Interestingly, there have been no previous reports of B. fragilis being isolated from the vagina of giant pandas.

pmc-12449732.title: Costs of 4 Months of Rifampin Versus 2 Months of Double-dose Rifampin for Tuberculosis Infection: Post-Hoc Analysis of a Phase 2b Randomized Trial
pmc-12449732.creator: Kamila Romanowski, Yen Pham Ngoc, Leila Barss, Elias Jabbour, James C Johnston, Hansen Herman, Richard Long, Lika Apriani, Greg Fox, Dick Menzies, Jonathon R Campbell
pmc-12449732.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundCost is an important consideration when implementing tuberculosis preventive treatment regimens (TPT). We used data from a phase 2b randomized trial of TPT to estimate overall cost and key drivers of costs for two TPT regimens.MethodsWe did a post-hoc analysis of 915 participants aged ≥10 years who were randomized 1:1 to 2 rifampin-based regimens: a four-month daily regimen at 10 mg/kg (4R10) and a 2-month daily regimen at 20 mg/kg (2R20; 461 participants).

pmc-12469510.title: Effect of a School-Based Physical Activity and Multi-Micronutrient Supplementation Intervention on Cognitive Function and Academic Achievement Among Schoolchildren in Tanzania: Secondary Outcome from the KaziAfya Cluster-Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-12469510.creator: Elihaika G Minja, Emmanuel C Mrimi, Winfrida P Mponzi, Johanna Beckmann, Marceline F Finda, Fredros O Okumu, Kurt Z Long, Christin Lang, Jürg Utzinger, Markus Gerber, Guglielmo Duranti
pmc-12469510.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: Physical activity (PA) and adequate micronutrient intake are essential for brain development and may influence cognitive function and academic achievement. However, few large-scale studies have assessed the combined effects of PA and multi-micronutrient supplementation (MMNS) in school-age children. Methods: A cluster-randomized placebo-controlled trial in four peri-urban Tanzanian schools assigned children to one of four groups: (i) PA alone; (ii) MMNS alone; (iii) PA plus MMNS; or (iv) placebo.

pmc-12472011.title: Formability and Electromagnetic Performance Comparison of Fe-P-Based SMC and Fe-5.0 wt.%Si Powders
pmc-12472011.creator: Seongsu Kang, Seonbong Lee
pmc-12472011.description: This study investigates the comparative applicability of Somaloy 700HR 5P and Fe-5.0 wt.%Si powders for axial flux permanent magnet (AFPM) motor cores in low-speed electric vehicles. Optimal forming conditions were derived through Taguchi-based simulations, considering corner radius, forming temperature, and forming speed, followed by prototype fabrication and validation.

pmc-12534995.title: The burden and determinants of intimate partner violence against reproductive-age women in four East African countries: evidence from 2021/2023 DHS dataset
pmc-12534995.creator: Gebresilassie Tadesse, Girum Nakie, Gidey Rtbey, Techilo Tinsae, Setegn Fentahun, Fantahun Andualem, Mulualem Kelebie, Yilkal Abebaw Wassie, Tigist Kifle Tsegaw, Getasew Kibralew
pmc-12534995.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIntimate Partner Violence (IPV) remains a critical public health and human rights issue, disproportionately affecting women in low-resource settings. Despite various interventions, IPV persists in East Africa due to entrenched gender norms, economic dependence, and weak law enforcement. This study aimed to determine the prevalence and associated factors of IPV among reproductive-age women in East Africa using recent Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) data.MethodsA multilevel analysis was conducted using DHS datasets from Kenya, Madagascar, Mozambique, and Tanzania (2021–2023).

pmc-12556043.title: Demographic and Epidemiological Transitions Across Africa: A Regional Policy Perspective
pmc-12556043.creator: F Ciccacci, F Basile, C Iazzolino, M Cicala, M Carestia, C Mosconi, C De Santo, P Germano, G Liotta, S Orlando
pmc-12556043.description: BackgroundAfrica is undergoing demographic and epidemiological transitions marked by population growth and a shift from communicable to non-communicable diseases (NCDs). These transitions vary by region and impact public health priorities. This study compares demographic and disease trends across five African regions to inform policy.MethodsWe conducted a descriptive study using secondary data.

pmc-12693496.title: Computational Analysis of Thermal Performance of Heat Sinks with Foam Structures
pmc-12693496.creator: Welteji Iticha, Tomasz Stręk
pmc-12693496.description: Ensuring efficient heat transfer to maintain optimal system performance is crucial in modern electronics owing to the rise of artificial intelligence. In the last few decades, scholars have explored various strategies for enhancing electronic device thermal management, focusing on the effects of fin shape, dimension, and spacing on heat transfer efficiency.

pmc-13227762.title: Phytoplasma infection induces changes in vibrational signals of Cacopsylla pyri: sex-specific shifts in frequency, amplitude, and timing
pmc-13227762.creator: Christina Koller, Ciara Hellweger, Andreas Jürgens, Jürgen Gross
pmc-13227762.description: The pear psyllid (Cacopsylla pyri), the main vector of ‘Candidatus Phytoplasma pyri’, relies on substrate-borne vibrational signals for mate recognition and duet coordination. As pathogens can alter insect communication, we examined whether phytoplasma infection alters key parameters of male and female mating signals. We used laser vibrometry on a standardised artificial substrate, as well as playbacks, to examine this.

pmc-13324126.title: Ginseng-containing Shentao Ruangan (STR) formula alleviates hepatic fibrosis via hepatocellular Nrf2-ROS-TGF-β axis regulating hepatocyte-HSC crosstalk: Integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and multi-tiered validation
pmc-13324126.creator: Shangyi Huang, Ruisheng Zhou, Jing Li, Yi Zheng, Lunwei Yang, Tianqi Gao, Yi Yuan, Dailin Wu, Yafei Shi, Dayong Zheng, Daihan Zhou, Ying Tang
pmc-13324126.description: BackgroundThe ginseng-containing Shentao Ruangan (STR) formula is clinically used for chronic liver conditions, including hepatic fibrosis. Guided by traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) principles, it targets the “deficiency leading to accumulation (Xu Sun Sheng Ji)" pathology in hepatic fibrosis via the “strengthening healthy qi and dispelling pathogenic factors (Fu Zheng Qu Xie)" mechanism.

pmc-13382166.title: A Chinese infant with CACNA1C p.C1021R variant expands clinical phenotype of CACNA1C-related disorder
pmc-13382166.creator: Congshan Jiang, Yafei Zhou, Siyu Zhang, Xiaoxiao Lu, Xia Li, Yanmin Zhang
pmc-13382166.description: CACNA1C-related disorder (CRD), a severe multisystem disorder caused by variants of CACNA1C gene, presents significant diagnostic and management challenges due to its rarity and variable expressivity. This study leverages a detailed longitudinal case report and comprehensive literature review to expand the phenotypic spectrum of CRD with Timothy syndrome (TS) features associated with the CACNA1C NM_001129830.1: c.3061 T > C (p.

pmc-13479987.title: Electronic health record adaptation and innovation among healthcare professionals in hospitals: an integrative framework based on a systematic review
pmc-13479987.creator: Judith Engels, Annet de Lange, Rogier van de Wetering, Jol Stoffers, Joris Van Ruysseveldt, Maitta Spronken
pmc-13479987.description: BackgroundWorldwide, many hospitals have adopted an Electronic Health Record (EHR) and are currently in the post-implementation phase. To exploit EHRs to their full potential, healthcare professionals must continuously engage in adaptive behaviors to cope with (changes and updates in) EHR systems, and explore existing and novel EHR functionalities.

pmc-13618694.title: Aphasia among Medicare fee for service beneficiaries: initial encounter for services and discharge disposition
pmc-13618694.creator: Charles Ellis, Molly Jacobs, Marcelo Perraillon, Karen Hegland, Robert McGowan, Anouk Grubaugh, Richard Lindrooth
pmc-13618694.description: Background:Studies report that 25–50% of stroke survivors in the United States experience aphasia. This study aimed to characterize where services for aphasia were initiated and the discharge disposition among fee-for-service (FFS) Medicare beneficiaries.Methods:Data included 100% of FFS Medicare claims for Home Health Agency (HHA), Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF), Inpatient, Outpatient, and Carrier files.

uslaw-usc-t7-s3156.creator: United States Congress
